prompt: What was the military rank of the employer of the astronomer who discovered the globular cluster of stars called NGC 644

content:

id: What teammates were inducted into the college football hall
prompt: What teammates were inducted into the college football hall of fame who played the same year as the first Native America
gold: Gus Welch, and William "Lone Star" Dietz.
content:
The Olympian was **Jim Thorpe**, who won gold in 1912. He played football for Carlisle in 1907–08 and 1911–12. ([Olympic Museum](https://usopm.org/jim-thorpe/); [Football Foundation](https://footballfoundation.org/honors/hall-of-fame/jim-thorpe/1264?path=football))

His Hall of Fame teammates were:

- [Albert Exendine](https://footballfoundation.org/honors/hall-of-fame/albert-exendine/1217?path=football) — played with Thorpe in 1907.
- [Gus Welch](https://footballfoundation.org/honors/college-football-hall-of-fame/gus-welch/1265) — played with him in 1911 and 1912.
- [Joe Guyon](https://www.cfbhall.com/inductees/joe-guyon-1971/) — played with him in 1912.
- [William “Lone Star” Dietz](https://wsucougars.com/william-lone-star-dietz-selected-to-college-football-hall-of-fame) — played with him in 1911 and was inducted as a coach. ([Team record](https://carlisleindian.dickinson.edu/images/football-team-1911-1912))

FINAL ANSWER: Albert Exendine, Gus Welch, Joe Guyon, William “Lone Star” Dietz

id: Which American high school can boast of an alumnus for whom
prompt: Which American high school can boast of an alumnus for whom the following is true: -Was inducted into the Pro Football H

No school satisfies the clues **literally**. The intended answer appears to be [Kathleen High School in Lakeland, Florida](https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ray-receives-first-hall-of-fame-honor-7747043), attended by Ray Lewis. He entered the [Hall of Fame in 2018](https://www.profootballhof.com/players/ray-lewis) after debuting in the Ravens’ [inaugural 1996 season](https://www.baltimoreravens.com/team/history/baltimore-football).

FINAL ANSWER: Pope Sylvester I

id: What is the percentage increase of total deaths of Japanese

content:
Using the upper ends of published estimates:

- **World War II:** 3,100,000 military and civilian deaths. [Source](https://www.nationalww2museum.org/students-teachers/student-resources/research-starters/research-starters-worldwide-deaths-world-war)

The increase is \((3,100,000 - 4,661) / 4,661 \times 100 \approx 66,409\%\). The figures are approximate and not perfectly comparable: the first includes missing personnel, while the second includes civilians.

FINAL ANSWER: Approximately 66,409%

Of the [three couriers](https://text-message.blogs.archives.gov/2014/03/11/hitlers-political-testament-part-ii/), only [Heinz Lorenz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heinz_Lorenz) died after 1980, in 1985. [Wilhelm Zander](https://ww2gravestone.com/people/zander-wilhelm/) died in 1974, and [Willy Johannmeyer](https://archive-cat.chch.ox.ac.uk/names/8af9b3f6-2c9b-4e2e-8e9e-dd71b8af2fc3) died in 1970.

FINAL ANSWER: 1

id: What was the word that featured the least in the longest rec
prompt: What was the word that featured the least in the longest recorded quotation by the chimpanzee named after the recipient
content:
The 2011 prize went to [Noam Chomsky](https://sydneypeacefoundation.org.au/peace-prize-recipients/2011-professor-noam-chomsky/), after whom the chimpanzee Nim Chimpsky was named. Nim’s [longest recorded utterance](https://languagelog.ldc.upenn.edu/nll/?p=3369) contained “you” once; every other word appeared at least three times. The naming is confirmed by the [Los Angeles Times](https://www.latimes.com/science/la-sci-sundance-nim-chimpsky-20110122-story.html).

FINAL ANSWER: you

prompt: When Taylor Swift first released her studio album "1989," how many studio albums had Katy Perry already released?
content:
Swift released [*1989* on October 27, 2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_(album)). By then, Perry had released [four studio albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy_Perry_discography), including her debut, *Katy Hudson*, under her birth name.

id: What band had a male lead singer born on the day Mohammad Mo
prompt: What band had a male lead singer born on the day Mohammad Mosaddegh announced the dissolution of the Iranian parliament?
content:
A [contemporary report](https://www.nytimes.com/1953/08/16/archives/mossadegh-terms-majlis-dissolved-premier-asks-shah-to-order-new.html) said parliament was considered dissolved on August 15, but Mossadegh [formally announced its dissolution](https://www.mohammadmossadegh.com/biography/august-16-1953/) on August 16, 1953.

That day, [James “J.T.” Taylor](https://www.iheart.com/artist/james-jt-taylor-30009354/), a future lead singer of **Kool & the Gang**, was born.

FINAL ANSWER: Kool & the Gang

id: What was the age difference between the inventor of Barbie a
prompt: What was the age difference between the inventor of Barbie and the inventor of Hot Wheels?
content:
Barbie creator [Ruth Handler](https://www.biography.com/inventors/a44446358/who-created-barbie-ruth-handler) was born on November 4, 1916. Her husband, Hot Wheels inventor [Elliot Handler](https://www.latimes.com/local/obituaries/la-me-elliot-handler-20110723-story.html), was born on April 9, 1916.

prompt: Little River Canyon National Preserve has three waterfalls, one of which is the tallest in Alabama. How much shorter is
content:
[Graces High Falls](https://home.nps.gov/liri/planyourvisit/waterfalls.htm) is 133 feet high. [Colonial Creek Falls](https://www.worldwaterfalldatabase.com/waterfall/Colonial-Creek-Falls-4738), the tallest recorded in the continental US, is approximately 2,568 feet high—a surveyed figure that replaced an older estimate.

2,568 − 133 = **2,435 feet**.

prompt: Of all states within New England in the United States, which had a population between 400,000 and 800,000 in 1920?
gold: Of the 6 states within New England, Maine, New Hampshire, and Rhode Island had populations between 400,000 and 800,000 in 1920.
content:
The [1920 census](https://www2.census.gov/prod2/statcomp/documents/1925-02.pdf) recorded three New England states in that range:

- New Hampshire: 443,083

id: Two famous modernist writers were born and died on the same
prompt: Two famous modernist writers were born and died on the same year. Who were they, which of them was alive for the longest
gold: Virginia Woolf and James Joyce. Virginia Woolf lived 82 days longer.
content:
- [Virginia Woolf](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Virginia-Woolf): January 25, 1882 – March 28, 1941.
- [James Joyce](https://www.britannica.com/biography/James-Joyce): February 2, 1882 – January 13, 1941.

Woolf was born 8 days earlier and died 74 days later, so she lived **82 days longer**.

FINAL ANSWER: Virginia Woolf and James Joyce; Virginia Woolf lived 82 days longer.

id: Give me the difference in time, measured in hours not days,
prompt: Give me the difference in time, measured in hours not days, between the first solo woman to thru-hike the Appalachian Tr
content:

Jennifer Pharr Davis’s 2011 individual record took **1,115⅓ hours**, though she had a support crew and companions for parts of the hike. [Source](https://fastestknowntime.com/fkt/jennifer-pharr-davis-appalachian-trail-2011-07-31)

prompt: I'm thinking of a painting. It was done by the same man who painted The Anti-Slavery Society Convention in the 1840's. T
content:
The likely answer is **The Mock Election** (1827), by Benjamin Robert Haydon. It depicts an election staged by prisoners in King’s Bench Prison. Haydon also painted [The Anti-Slavery Society Convention](https://www.npg.org.uk/collections/search/portrait/mw00028/The-Anti-Slavery-Society-Convention-1840) in 1841. ([Royal Collection Trust](https://www.rct.uk/collection/405824/the-mock-election))

Another possibility is his related painting [Chairing the Member](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-britain/display/historic-early-modern-british-art/1770).

FINAL ANSWER: The Mock Election
